key_insight: The paper introduces second-order, Lagrange-multiplier-based optimization flows that add inertial acceleration while preserving pseudo-energy dissipation, yielding stable convergence to stationary points in nonconvex problems.
engineering_relevance: These methods can improve training robustness and optimization quality for scientific machine learning models such as PINNs and DeepONets, especially when standard first-order methods get stuck or are sensitive to learning-rate choice.
method: Linear LM-based second-order flow for unconstrained nonconvex optimization
Variable and operator splitting version for accelerated iterative updates
Relaxed and adaptive variants to prevent multiplier degeneration and tune time steps automatically
evidence_signal: The abstract reports extensive numerical tests on function optimization and PDE benchmarks, including PINN and DeepONet training, showing improved escape from local minima, high accuracy, and strong robustness to initial learning-rate choice.
watch_item: The approach adds algorithmic complexity and extra tuning/implementation details around multiplier updates and adaptive step control, which may affect practical deployment.
paper_title: Several Accelerated and Stable Pseudo-Energy-Dissipative Lagrange Multiplier Methods based on Second-order Flow and Variable Splitting
